title: SAFE: Multitask Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models
models: OpenVLA (LIBERO fine-tuned; Open-X Magic Soup++ pretrained on real WidowX)
pi0* (open reproduction, SimplerEnv Google Robot and WidowX)
action_head: mixed: discrete action tokens (OpenVLA, pi0-FAST) and flow/diffusion action expert (pi0, pi0*); features taken from the last layer before logits or before the velocity projection
methods: supervised probe on last-layer features (1-2 layer MLP with cumulative score, or 1-layer LSTM)
functional conformal prediction for time-varying thresholds
baselines: token uncertainty, sample consistency, embedding distances, RND, LogpZO, STAC
question: Can a single failure detector trained on VLA internal features from seen tasks detect failures early on unseen tasks, for several VLA architectures?
key_findings: t-SNE of pi0-FAST last-layer features on LIBERO-10 shows failed rollouts from different tasks drifting into a shared 'failure zone' (Fig. 1); for OpenVLA failures form small scattered blobs, and on the real Franka successes and failures are not visibly separable (App. C.1).

Simulation ROC-AUC averaged over 4 benchmarks (Table 1, 3 seeds/splits): SAFE-MLP 81.43 seen / 78.00 unseen, SAFE-LSTM 82.26 / 77.04; best single-sample baseline on unseen is Cosine k-NN at 73.93; paper reports SAFE beats best baseline by 4-5% on unseen tasks.
SAFE does not win everywhere: on pi0 LIBERO unseen, SAFE-MLP 73.27 vs Mahalanobis 74.31 and gripper total variation 75.19; on pi0-FAST LIBERO unseen, STAC (10 samples) 85.31 vs SAFE-LSTM 84.48.
Token-uncertainty baselines (max/avg prob, entropy) are near chance (about 44-69 ROC-AUC across settings), matching the LLM UQ literature.

Real robot (Fig. 6a, 5 seeds/splits): pi0-FAST Franka SAFE-MLP 86.76 seen / 64.16 unseen (best baseline unseen Euclid k-NN 60.27); OpenVLA WidowX SAFE-MLP 89.11 seen / 88.42 unseen vs Mahalanobis 82.37 / 70.00.

Ablation (Table 7, real Franka): image-only DINOv2+CLIP features give SAFE-LSTM 77.09 seen / 59.65 unseen vs VLA features 77.27 / 58.70; only the MLP variant shows a clear VLA-feature advantage (86.76 vs 76.36 seen, 64.16 vs 58.43 unseen).
More training tasks generally help unseen performance on OpenVLA LIBERO (Table 6): SAFE-MLP unseen 63.76 with 1 task, 73.47 with 7.
Overhead: SAFE-LSTM has 2.3M parameters and adds 0.73 ms vs pi0 inference of 149 ms; multi-sample methods make pi0 152% and pi0-FAST 221% slower for 10 samples.
SAFE-MLP predicts 40% of pi0-FAST LIBERO failures after the first timestep (App. C.3), i.e. many failures are predictable from the initial state.

evidence.setting: both (LIBERO-10 and SimplerEnv simulation; real Franka with pi0-FAST-DROID and real WidowX with OpenVLA)
benchmarks: SimplerEnv (Google Robot and WidowX, 4 tasks each)
evidence.scale: LIBERO-10: 10 tasks x 50 rollouts per VLA, 3 tasks held out as unseen, 60/40 train/val split on seen. Franka: 13 tasks x 30 successful + 30 failed rollouts, 3 unseen. WidowX: 532 rollouts (244 success, 288 fail), 2 of 8 tasks unseen. Sim results averaged over 3 seeds with different task splits, real over 5.
evidence.statistics: partial: means over 3 or 5 seed/split runs; standard deviations in App. Table 8; no significance tests or CIs
evidence.baselines: token max/avg prob and entropy; sample-consistency (action total variation, cluster entropy, 10 samples); embedding distances (Mahalanobis, k-NN Euclid/cosine, PCA-KMeans); RND and LogpZO (FAIL-Detect); STAC and STAC-Single; DINOv2/CLIP image features (ablation)

causal_validation: None. The detector is a correlational probe; no ablation or steering along the success/failure direction is done. The authors only suggest steering as future work (App. F.3).
closed_loop: Detection is evaluated offline on recorded closed-loop rollouts (no intervention during execution). The detector never triggers a stop or recovery in the loop, so the downstream benefit of detection is not measured.
limitations_stated: Only manipulation; unclear generalization across embodiments, sim-to-real or to action-less video.
Only last-layer features; how to aggregate across layers is open.
Needs deployment and collection of successful and failed rollouts to train the detector.
Conformal guarantee assumes exchangeability that fails when calibrating on seen and testing on unseen tasks; TNR falls below 1 - alpha on 3 of 5 benchmarks (App. C.2).
Human failure-time annotation is ambiguous for freezing and repeated-grasp failures.
critique: The 'VLA features know about failure' claim is weakened by the paper's own Table 7: generic DINOv2+CLIP image features match VLA features for the LSTM on real Franka, so much of the signal may be visual scene state rather than policy-internal knowledge; the text nonetheless says VLA features win 'by a large margin'.
Unseen-task generalization on real Franka is weak (best ROC-AUC 64.16); the strong cross-task story rests mostly on simulation and the 8-task WidowX setup.
Only the final layer is probed and features are aggregated by mean/first/last selected on validation data, so the paper says nothing about where in the network failure information first appears.
Unseen tasks come from the same suite (LIBERO-10, same embodiment and scenes), so 'unseen task' is a mild shift; no visual or embodiment shift is tested.
Good that the authors fix rollout length per task to stop detectors from just counting time, a shortcut later papers in this batch should be checked for.
Results across 3 seeds with per-split variation and no tests; several margins over baselines (1-4 points) are within the reported std ranges.
one_line: A small MLP or LSTM on the last-layer features of OpenVLA, pi0 and pi0-FAST flags task failure on held-out tasks better than uncertainty and OOD baselines, but generic image features do nearly as well on the real robot and nothing is tested causally.
